input.rationale: Interpreted the real-cluster receipt for the stale-configuration election consequence and integrated it into the parent account. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e parsed three events from the live five-node cluster and evaluated all seven comparisons: the restarted node reports the stale membership instead of the committed one (violated, witness index 1), the stale-configured node reaches Leader while holding two of the five voters (violated, index 2), the cluster has two leaders (violated, index 2), the two leaders commit different entries at the same index and term (violated, index 2), the minority leader commits an entry (violated, index 2), while the in-partition control node with the current configuration never leads (holds, index 2) and the rest of the cluster keeps reporting the current five-voter membership (holds, index 2). The child question now has both an experiment-level and a question-level interpretation; the parent account's pending-election limitation is replaced by this confirmed witness with joint_history explaining why the two receipts belong to one behaviour chain, and the quorum fact gains this receipt as a recorded execution.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.
knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

interpretations.rationale: The predicates declared for this cluster are contradicted by valid witnesses. Admission index 0 establishes the setup: snapshot index 6 with configuration {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8 covering that entry, and A reporting the five-voter membership before the restart. After A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from its own stores (index 1) it reports {A,B,C} with last_applied 8, i.e. it holds the committed five-voter entry in its log and still uses the three-voter membership. With the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} (index 2): A is Leader in the two-voter partition (stale_config_node_is_leader true, minority_leaders A, terms A:3,C:3), B is Leader on the other side (majority_leaders B, terms B:3,D:3,E:3), so leader_count is 2 rather than 1; both leaders accept and commit a command (minority_write_committed true, majority_write_committed by the same operand on the other side), and both commit at index 11 in term 3 with different payloads (minority_write_data minority-write, majority_write_data majority-write, conflicting_commits true). The in-partition control holds: C, whose configuration is the current one, never becomes leader in the same two-voter partition (index 2, comparison 5 holds), which is the expected behaviour when the quorum is three, and the rest of the cluster still reports {A,B,C,D,E} (comparison 6 holds), so the two sides lead with different membership views. Mechanism: the restart keeps the snapshot membership (api.go 610-620 with the replay from api.go 724-753 advancing lastApplied), the candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), and voters grant from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), so two votes suffice where the current membership requires three; the persisted commit index that drives the replay only exists because the deployment ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Limits: the control used here is the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, not a no-feature restart of the same node, so the file's original control variant is unexecuted; A is shut down gracefully rather than crashed and only in-memory stores are used; the partition is transport-only and lasts for the observation window, so the later loss of the minority entry after healing is not observed.
counterevidence: C, in the same partition with the current configuration, cannot win because it needs three votes, which confirms the election difference comes from the configuration view and not from the partition alone.

The majority side keeps the current membership and elects its own leader, so the observation is two legitimate-looking leadership states over one cluster rather than a single side failing to make progress.
limitations: No no-feature restart control of the same node was executed in this cluster; the causal contrast is the in-partition sibling C plus the earlier feature-off construction experiment.
A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact, so no crash or storage-fault path is covered.
The two leaders are observed while partitioned; the healing step and the resulting loss of the minority entry are not executed.
Only in-memory stores, default configuration and scaled timeouts were used.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay does win an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log, and the rest of the cluster elects its own leader at the same time. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e shows the whole chain on stores produced by normal operations: the config entry at index 8 (five voters) is committed and stored while node A's snapshot stays at index 6 (three voters) and A's stored commit index is 8, the restarted A reports {A,B,C}, the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} leaves A leader of two voters against a quorum of three and B leader of the other three, and both leaders commit a different entry at index 11 in term 3. The mechanism is the parent question's defect plus the quorum rule: candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) while voters admit requests from their own view (raft.go 1660-1680), so the stale node needs two votes where three are required. Scope: the witness is one cluster, one partition window and in-memory stores with a graceful shutdown rather than a crash; the no-feature restart control variant of the discriminator was replaced by the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, which cannot lead for the same partition. Also open: whether the minority entry is dropped once the partition heals, and how long a stale node can keep acting as leader while it can still reach a stale majority.
counterevidence: The control sibling C in the same partition never leads, so the partition alone does not explain the leadership change.
The stale node's log is complete and committed up to index 8, so its election is not explained by a lagging log.
limitations: Single cluster, single partition window, in-memory stores and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
The intended no-feature restart control is unexecuted; the in-partition sibling stands in for it.
Post-healing fate of the conflicting entry at index 11 term 3 is not observed.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum, and that stale view is sufficient for it to become leader with two votes where the current configuration requires three, producing two concurrent leaders and conflicting commits. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed configuration entry, which is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. Receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 gives the configuration and quorum state on harness-supplied stores (feature on: lastApplied 7, configuration index 1 with {A,B,C}, quorum 2, live node reporting {A,B,C}; feature off: configuration index 6 with {A,B,C,D,E}, quorum 3; indices 3 and 5 against 1), and receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e gives the operational consequence in a live five-node cluster (indices 1 and 2): the restarted node reports {A,B,C}, leads a two-voter partition, the other three voters elect their own leader, and both commit different entries at index 11 in term 3. The persisted commit index that drives the replay only exists because the deployment ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403), so the divergence is the feature's own effect rather than an externally fabricated store state. Remaining limits: the restart is graceful with in-memory stores and a transport-only partition, the minority entry's post-healing fate is unobserved, no no-feature restart control was executed in the cluster (the in-partition sibling C and the earlier feature-off construction carry that contrast), and the stale membership's long-run persistence under an active leader is still argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries rather than observed over a long window. The first filed experiment's receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e remains a retained channel failure with no evaluated comparison.
counterevidence: The node stores the newer committed configuration entry and replays it to the FSM, so repair through a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot remains possible.

A deployment that never ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled stores commit index 0, in which case the scan covers the entry and no divergence occurs; the defect needs the feature enabled before the restart.
The in-partition control C, which holds the current configuration, cannot lead in the same partition, so the partition alone does not explain the outcome.
limitations: The stale membership's long-run persistence under an active leader is not observed; it rests on the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries (raft.go 1526-1553) and the absence of another refresh path.
Both experiments use in-memory stores, scaled timeouts and a graceful shutdown of the restarted node rather than a crash.
The cluster witness uses a transport-only partition over one observation window and does not follow the conflicting entry past healing.
No no-feature restart control was executed inside the cluster; the contrast comes from the in-partition sibling and the feature-off construction.
interpretations.joint_history: The two receipts are different fixed experiments over the same defect chain: the first constructs the restart state directly in stores supplied by the harness and reads the resulting configuration, quorum and FSM queue; the second produces a comparable state through normal operations (bootstrap, election, membership change, user snapshot, restart) and then observes the election outcome. They are compatible because both restart the same node identity A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from stores whose snapshot configuration is {A,B,C} while a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} sits above the snapshot and the persisted commit index covers it (index 2 of the first receipt and index 0 of the second), and both observe the restarted node reporting {A,B,C} (index 3 and index 1 respectively). No values are combined across receipts; each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft's post-restore configuration scan iterates index from max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 up to the last log index and calls processConfigurationLogEntry for every entry in that range, so configuration entries at or below the scan start are never processed into r.configurations during construction.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a Raft instance from retained log/stable/snapshot state; the scan runs after restoreSnapshot and after restoreFromCommittedLogs, and before skipStartup returns control to the caller.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets the in-memory commit index from store.GetCommitIndex() (clamped to the log's last index) and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs enqueues the corresponding commitTuples on fsmMutateCh and then sets lastApplied to that index.
knowledge.conditions: Called during NewRaft, after snapshot restore and before runFSM is started; the log store must implement CommitTrackingLogStore or NewRaft returns ErrIncompatibleLogStore.

knowledge.statement: Outside NewRaft, r.configurations is updated only by the AppendEntries path for entries that are not already present as duplicates with the same term, by processConfigurationLogEntry for those new entries, and by installSnapshot (which sets both latest and committed from the snapshot request); processLogs and the FSM apply path never update the configuration.
knowledge.conditions: Running follower/leader loops on the main thread; duplicate entries (index at or below lastLogIdx with matching term) are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry is reached.

knowledge.statement: A node's election quorum and voter eligibility are computed only from r.configurations.latest (quorumSize counts Voters in latest; the candidate threshold is grantedVotes >= quorumSize, and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's own latest configuration), so a node holding a configuration older than its own committed log counts a smaller voter set and requires fewer votes to become leader.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

The feature's documented purpose (config.go 243-255) is to replay committed logs into the FSM, so changing the scan start index may have been intentional; the account rests on the resulting membership state, not on the intent.
limitations: The experiment supplies the durable state (snapshot at index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log entry 6 = LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, StageCommitIndex(7)) rather than producing it with a live cluster, so the fixture asserts reachability by source reasoning rather than by an executed prefix.
The minority-quorum election consequence is derived from source (quorumSize/vote admission) and has no executed multi-node witness yet.

The persistence of the stale configuration is argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries and from the absence of any other configuration refresh path; it was not observed over a long-running node with an active leader.
Only the two in-memory store types and the module's own constructors were used; no repository test suite and no on-disk log store were exercised.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate for this experiment is that a node constructed from these stores uses the membership of the committed configuration entry that sits in its own log: entries at index 6 carry LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} with the log store reporting commit index 7. In the feature-on construction (event index 3, correlated to admission index 2) the assertion is contradicted: lastApplied is 7, latest_config_index is 1, latest_config_ids is A,B,C and quorum_size is 2, i.e. the node kept the snapshot's membership and sized its election quorum from it. The identical fixture with RestoreCommittedLogs off (event index 1, admission index 0) satisfies the same assertion (latest_config_index 6, latest_config_ids A,B,C,D,E, quorum_size 3), and it is the only difference between the two constructions, so the eager replay rather than the fixture explains the divergence: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753) which advances lastApplied to 7 (raft.go 1361-1362, comparison index 4 holds for the feature-on node and index 5 for the control at 5), and the configuration scan then starts at max(5,7)+1 = 8 (api.go 610-620), leaving index 6 unprocessed by processConfigurationLogEntry. The running node reports the same stale membership through the public API while it campaigns (event index 5, admission index 4, comparison index 6), so this is live node state and not only a constructor artefact. Consequences that follow from the same recorded operands: candidate admission and quorum come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), so the restarted node requires two votes instead of three, while peers admit its vote request from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680). Limits retained: the fixture supplies the durable state instead of producing it through a live cluster, so fixture reachability rests on source reasoning; the minority-quorum election itself is not executed here and is the registered follow-on question; persistence of the stale membership is argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries (raft.go 1526-1553) and the absence of any other configuration refresh path rather than observed over a long-running node; NoSnapshotRestoreOnStart, on-disk log stores and protocol-version variations were not exercised. The earlier receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e remains a retained channel failure with zero parsed results and supports no comparison.
counterevidence: The feature-on node does hold the newer committed configuration entry: one FSM batch covering indexes 6 and 7 is queued, so the stale membership is an unprocessed entry, not a missing one.

The replayed entries include the configuration entry but processLogs treats it as an ordinary FSM commit, which is consistent with the documented purpose of RestoreCommittedLogs and leaves the scan start index as the only observable difference from the control.
limitations: The fixture supplies the snapshot, log entries and persisted commit index rather than producing them with a live cluster, so the belief that a follower can reach this state rests on source reasoning.

result.summary: Interpreted the real-cluster receipt and integrated it into the parent account. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e parsed cleanly and all seven comparisons evaluated: the restarted node reports {A,B,C} instead of the committed {A,B,C,D,E} (violated, witness index 1), the stale-configured node reaches Leader holding two of five voters (violated, index 2), the cluster shows two leaders (violated, index 2), the two leaders commit different entries at the same index 11 in term 3 (violated, index 2), the minority leader commits an entry (violated, index 2), while the in-partition control node with the current configuration never leads and the rest of the cluster keeps reporting {A,B,C,D,E} (both hold, index 2). The child question therefore has an experiment-level violated/asserted interpretation and a question-level explained/asserted account; the parent question's interpretation was revised to replace its pending-election limitation with this confirmed split-brain witness, with joint_history explaining how the two receipts (supplied-store construction and live-cluster witness) belong to one behaviour chain, and the quorum fact gained the new receipt as a recorded execution. Limits now recorded: no no-feature restart control inside the cluster, graceful shutdown instead of a crash, in-memory stores and a transport-only partition over one window, unobserved post-healing fate of the conflicting entry, and stale-membership persistence still argued from the AppendEntries duplicate-skip rather than observed over a long window. Incomplete: a healing-phase successor experiment to observe whether the same-index/same-term divergent entries survive unrepairable, and the earlier registered constructor replay-backpressure question.

knowledge.conditions: Election handling on the candidate and voter sides (runCandidate, requestVote); r.configurations.latest is not reconciled with the node's log at any other time.

knowledge.statement: The persisted commit index that RestoreCommittedLogs later reads is written only by tryStageCommitIndex, which returns immediately unless r.RestoreCommittedLogs is true; its callers are dispatchLogs on a leader (staging the commit index as of before the new entries are stored) and the AppendEntries path on a follower (staging min(LeaderCommitIndex, last new entry index)). A node that committed entries while the feature was disabled leaves a stored commit index of 0, so a later restart with the feature enabled replays nothing even though its log is long.
knowledge.conditions: Requires a log store implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the guard is on the running instance's RestoreCommittedLogs value, so mixed deployments (feature off, then on) do not have a persisted commit index to replay.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: when Config.RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store's persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go 724-753) reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 = commit+1 (api.go 610-620), so index 6 of the fixture - a committed LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} that the node stores and that the FSM is asked to apply - is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. The node therefore keeps the snapshot's membership {A,B,C} in both r.configurations.latest and r.configurations.committed (latest index 1). Because a candidate's threshold and a node's voter set come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) and vote requests are admitted based on the receiver's configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), the restarted node's election quorum is 2 instead of 3. The condition is not self-healing in the observed paths: duplicate entries are skipped before processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1526-1553), so a leader that already has this follower's log matched does not cause the entry to be re-processed, and the configurations are only refreshed by new entries or by an installed snapshot (raft.go 1955-1962). Local construction feedback on the draft harness returned exactly the predicted difference (feature off: lastApplied 5, latest {A,B,C,D,E} at index 6, quorum 3; feature on: lastApplied 7, latest {A,B,C} at index 1, quorum 2, and the live case reporting {A,B,C} through GetConfiguration); the retained execution is the basis for changing this account, so the account is conditional on the filed experiment's receipt. Counterevidence and limits: the fixture's log and snapshot indexes are supplied rather than produced by a live node, the multi-node election with a minority of the true configuration was not executed, and the node still stores the newer configuration entry in its log (so a reviewer may argue repair is possible through a later entry or an installed snapshot); the abandoned-write consequence therefore stays a source-reasoned consequence until a multi-node witness exists. The second registered question (constructor replay backpressure) is independent of this account.
counterevidence: The node does store the newer committed configuration entry in its log (the FSM batch is queued for index 6/7), so the stale membership is not a missing entry but an unprocessed one.

The feature's documented purpose (config.go 243-255) is to replay committed logs into the FSM, so changing the scan start index may have been intentional; the account rests on the resulting membership state, not on the intent.
limitations: The experiment supplies the durable state (snapshot at index 5 with configuration {A,B,C}, log entry 6 = LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E}, StageCommitIndex(7)) rather than producing it with a live cluster, so the fixture asserts reachability by source reasoning rather than by an executed prefix.
The minority-quorum election consequence is derived from source (quorumSize/vote admission) and has no executed multi-node witness yet.

The persistence of the stale configuration is argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries and from the absence of any other configuration refresh path; it was not observed over a long-running node with an active leader.
Only the two in-memory store types and the module's own constructors were used; no repository test suite and no on-disk log store were exercised.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate for this experiment is that a node constructed from these stores uses the membership of the committed configuration entry that sits in its own log: entries at index 6 carry LogConfiguration{A,B,C,D,E} with the log store reporting commit index 7. In the feature-on construction (event index 3, correlated to admission index 2) the assertion is contradicted: lastApplied is 7, latest_config_index is 1, latest_config_ids is A,B,C and quorum_size is 2, i.e. the node kept the snapshot's membership and sized its election quorum from it. The identical fixture with RestoreCommittedLogs off (event index 1, admission index 0) satisfies the same assertion (latest_config_index 6, latest_config_ids A,B,C,D,E, quorum_size 3), and it is the only difference between the two constructions, so the eager replay rather than the fixture explains the divergence: restoreFromCommittedLogs calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753) which advances lastApplied to 7 (raft.go 1361-1362, comparison index 4 holds for the feature-on node and index 5 for the control at 5), and the configuration scan then starts at max(5,7)+1 = 8 (api.go 610-620), leaving index 6 unprocessed by processConfigurationLogEntry. The running node reports the same stale membership through the public API while it campaigns (event index 5, admission index 4, comparison index 6), so this is live node state and not only a constructor artefact. Consequences that follow from the same recorded operands: candidate admission and quorum come only from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), so the restarted node requires two votes instead of three, while peers admit its vote request from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680). Limits retained: the fixture supplies the durable state instead of producing it through a live cluster, so fixture reachability rests on source reasoning; the minority-quorum election itself is not executed here and is the registered follow-on question; persistence of the stale membership is argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries (raft.go 1526-1553) and the absence of any other configuration refresh path rather than observed over a long-running node; NoSnapshotRestoreOnStart, on-disk log stores and protocol-version variations were not exercised. The earlier receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e remains a retained channel failure with zero parsed results and supports no comparison.
counterevidence: The feature-on node does hold the newer committed configuration entry: one FSM batch covering indexes 6 and 7 is queued, so the stale membership is an unprocessed entry, not a missing one.

The replayed entries include the configuration entry but processLogs treats it as an ordinary FSM commit, which is consistent with the documented purpose of RestoreCommittedLogs and leaves the scan start index as the only observable difference from the control.
limitations: The fixture supplies the snapshot, log entries and persisted commit index rather than producing them with a live cluster, so the belief that a follower can reach this state rests on source reasoning.
The election consequence (a stale-configured node winning with a minority of the current voter set) is not executed in this experiment; it is registered as the follow-on question.
Persistence of the stale membership until another configuration entry arrives was not observed on a long-running node with an active leader.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node uses the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620), above the committed configuration entry, which is therefore never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. Receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 confirms this end to end: with the feature on, lastApplied 7, latest configuration index 1 and membership {A,B,C}, quorum 2, and the running node reporting {A,B,C} through the public configuration API (indices 3 and 5); with the feature off on identical stores, latest configuration index 6 with {A,B,C,D,E} and quorum 3 (index 1); both controls for the mechanism operand and for the assertion hold (indices 1, 4, 5). The same operands show the node's election threshold coming from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) while peers admit votes from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), so the restarted node needs two votes where the current configuration requires three. Still open, and the reason this account stays scoped: the fixture is supplied rather than produced by a live cluster; the minority-quorum election has no executed witness (registered as the follow-on question); the persistence of the stale membership rests on the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries (raft.go 1526-1553) plus the absence of another refresh path rather than on a long-running observation; only in-memory stores and default configuration were used. The first filed experiment's receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e is retained as a channel failure (six invalid_observation lines, no evaluated comparison) and supports none of the claims above.
counterevidence: The node stores the newer committed configuration entry (one queued FSM batch for indexes 6 and 7), so repair through a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot is not excluded by these observations.

interpretations.rationale: The predicates declared for this cluster are contradicted by valid witnesses. Admission index 0 establishes the setup: snapshot index 6 with configuration {A,B,C}, committed configuration entry at index 8 with {A,B,C,D,E}, stored commit index 8 covering that entry, and A reporting the five-voter membership before the restart. After A is restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from its own stores (index 1) it reports {A,B,C} with last_applied 8, i.e. it holds the committed five-voter entry in its log and still uses the three-voter membership. With the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} (index 2): A is Leader in the two-voter partition (stale_config_node_is_leader true, minority_leaders A, terms A:3,C:3), B is Leader on the other side (majority_leaders B, terms B:3,D:3,E:3), so leader_count is 2 rather than 1; both leaders accept and commit a command (minority_write_committed true, majority_write_committed by the same operand on the other side), and both commit at index 11 in term 3 with different payloads (minority_write_data minority-write, majority_write_data majority-write, conflicting_commits true). The in-partition control holds: C, whose configuration is the current one, never becomes leader in the same two-voter partition (index 2, comparison 5 holds), which is the expected behaviour when the quorum is three, and the rest of the cluster still reports {A,B,C,D,E} (comparison 6 holds), so the two sides lead with different membership views. Mechanism: the restart keeps the snapshot membership (api.go 610-620 with the replay from api.go 724-753 advancing lastApplied), the candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096), and voters grant from their own configuration (raft.go 1660-1680), so two votes suffice where the current membership requires three; the persisted commit index that drives the replay only exists because the deployment ran with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled (raft.go 1393-1403). Limits: the control used here is the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, not a no-feature restart of the same node, so the file's original control variant is unexecuted; A is shut down gracefully rather than crashed and only in-memory stores are used; the partition is transport-only and lasts for the observation window, so the later loss of the minority entry after healing is not observed.
counterevidence: C, in the same partition with the current configuration, cannot win because it needs three votes, which confirms the election difference comes from the configuration view and not from the partition alone.

The majority side keeps the current membership and elects its own leader, so the observation is two legitimate-looking leadership states over one cluster rather than a single side failing to make progress.
limitations: No no-feature restart control of the same node was executed in this cluster; the causal contrast is the in-partition sibling C plus the earlier feature-off construction experiment.
A is shut down gracefully and its stores are reused intact, so no crash or storage-fault path is covered.
The two leaders are observed while partitioned; the healing step and the resulting loss of the minority entry are not executed.
Only in-memory stores, default configuration and scaled timeouts were used.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes. A node left with a stale configuration by the RestoreCommittedLogs replay does win an election with fewer votes than the configuration recorded in its own committed log, and the rest of the cluster elects its own leader at the same time. Receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e shows the whole chain on stores produced by normal operations: the config entry at index 8 (five voters) is committed and stored while node A's snapshot stays at index 6 (three voters) and A's stored commit index is 8, the restarted A reports {A,B,C}, the partition {A,C} | {B,D,E} leaves A leader of two voters against a quorum of three and B leader of the other three, and both leaders commit a different entry at index 11 in term 3. The mechanism is the parent question's defect plus the quorum rule: candidate threshold and voter set come from configurations.latest (raft.go 313-320, 1085-1096) while voters admit requests from their own view (raft.go 1660-1680), so the stale node needs two votes where three are required. Scope: the witness is one cluster, one partition window and in-memory stores with a graceful shutdown rather than a crash; the no-feature restart control variant of the discriminator was replaced by the in-partition sibling with the correct configuration, which cannot lead for the same partition. Also open: whether the minority entry is dropped once the partition heals, and how long a stale node can keep acting as leader while it can still reach a stale majority.
counterevidence: The control sibling C in the same partition never leads, so the partition alone does not explain the leadership change.
The stale node's log is complete and committed up to index 8, so its election is not explained by a lagging log.
limitations: Single cluster, single partition window, in-memory stores and a graceful shutdown rather than a crash.
The intended no-feature restart control is unexecuted; the in-partition sibling stands in for it.
Post-healing fate of the conflicting entry at index 11 term 3 is not observed.

interpretations.rationale: Current account: with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore whose persisted commit index covers a committed configuration entry newer than the node's last snapshot, NewRaft does not rebuild the node's configuration from that entry, so the restarted node keeps the snapshot's membership for candidate admission and election quorum, and that stale view is sufficient for it to become leader with two votes where the current configuration requires three, producing two concurrent leaders and conflicting commits. Basis: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the persisted commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil) (api.go 724-753); processLogs advances lastApplied to that index (raft.go 1361-1362); the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 610-620) above the committed configuration entry, which is never passed to processConfigurationLogEntry. Receipt f4adc58c4125434eb91cacf438a6da50 gives the configuration and quorum state on harness-supplied stores (feature on: lastApplied 7, configuration index 1 with {A,B,C}, quorum 2, live node reporting {A,B,C}; feature off: configuration index 6 with {A,B,C,D,E}, quorum 3; indices 3 and 5 against 1), and receipt b68f3d3a08b34cd6a27b76faeb0d2a3e gives the operational consequence in a live five-node cluster (indices 1 and 2): the restarted node reports {A,B,C}, leads a two-voter partition, the other three voters elect their own leader, and both commit different entries at index 11 in term 3. The persisted commit index that drives the replay only exists because the deployment ran with the feature enabled (raft.go 1393-1403), so the divergence is the feature's own effect rather than an externally fabricated store state. Remaining limits: the restart is graceful with in-memory stores and a transport-only partition, the minority entry's post-healing fate is unobserved, no no-feature restart control was executed in the cluster (the in-partition sibling C and the earlier feature-off construction carry that contrast), and the stale membership's long-run persistence under an active leader is still argued from the duplicate-skip in AppendEntries rather than observed over a long window. The first filed experiment's receipt 99718ab469974eb1ad40516efe7c999e remains a retained channel failure with no evaluated comparison.
counterevidence: The node stores the newer committed configuration entry and replays it to the FSM, so repair through a later configuration entry or an installed snapshot remains possible.

interpretations.joint_history: The two receipts are different fixed experiments over the same defect chain: the first constructs the restart state directly in stores supplied by the harness and reads the resulting configuration, quorum and FSM queue; the second produces a comparable state through normal operations (bootstrap, election, membership change, user snapshot, restart) and then observes the election outcome. They are compatible because both restart the same node identity A with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs from stores whose snapshot configuration is {A,B,C} while a committed configuration entry with {A,B,C,D,E} sits above the snapshot and the persisted commit index covers it (index 2 of the first receipt and index 0 of the second), and both observe the restarted node reporting {A,B,C} (index 3 and index 1 respectively). No values are combined across receipts; each comparison outcome is read from its own receipt.
